newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 7.0/7.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 7.0/7.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 7.0/7.5 percent, compared with an opening of 6.25 percent on Thursday morning, dealers said.
They said a sudden rebound in tom/next swaps seemed to help overnight money to improve slightly. Tom/next swaps rose to 1.0/1.2 points from par in the morning.
One Japanese bank dealer said some buying interest by state banks for rupiah up to one-week seemed to alert the market that liquidity might be on the way to stabilising.
"This might also have driven rates up slighly," he said.
However, longer-term rates remained low, with one-month money last given at 12.0 and three at 12.875 percent.
One state bank dealer said weekly tax payments due Friday were expected to be moderate.

Bank Indonesia offered overnight bilateral papers (SBIs) at six percent, 4-7 day at eight, eight-day at 9.5 percent, 11-15 day at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.75 percent, three at 12.5 percent, six at 12.75 and 12 at 13.00 percent.
Bond dealers said the market remained biddish, but the average yield was still hovering around 15.5 to 16.5 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 7.85 percent, compared with 7.27 percent on Tuesday.
